newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Basques to issue 18 bln pta in 10-yr bonds.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Basques to issue 18 bln pta in 10-yr bonds.

text.p: Spain's Basque region will offer 18 billion pesetas in 10-year bonds to domestic institutional investors this week, officials said on Tuesday.
This is the regional government's second Euskobonos issue this year and could see a spread of 10 basis points over bonos with the same maturity.
"On November 8 we will look at the banks' offer," Miguel Bengoechea, financial director of the regional government, told Reuters in a phone interview.
"I hope we pay less than 10 basis points over bonos".
Today the Spanish Treasury sold a new tranche of the 10-year benchmark at 111.246, with a minimun yield of 7.804 percent.
The Basque country is planning to close 1996 with a gross issue of 64 billion versus 80 billion pesetas in 1995.
In December the regional government is set to issue 21 billion pesetas in five-year bonds, aimed at retail investors.

Usually this region, which has the highest degree of financial autonomy in Spain for historic reasons, has tried not to sell its debt to foreign investors. It prefers not to have to reimburse the 25 percent witholding tax on interest.
"To place Euskobonos for domestic investors is cheaper for us," said Bengoechea.
The region is planning gross issues of 40 billion pesetas of 1997, he added.
According to the Bank of Spain, the Basque country had debt of 319 billion pesetas at the end of June this year.
